config.title: Form Library from Scratch

intro.title: Form Library from Scratch
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form library from scratch using Vue. You will learn how to create a reusable form component that manages input state and validation. The core concept is reactive state management with Vue's ref and computed properties. You will use Vue components, event handling, and conditional rendering to construct the form. By the end, you'll have a basic library that can handle form data and display validation messages.
intro.usecase: Form libraries are essential in modern web applications where user input drives functionality. You'll find them in e-commerce checkout flows, user registration systems, and admin dashboards where data validation and submission are critical. In Vue applications, custom form libraries power everything from multi-step onboarding wizards to complex data entry panels in enterprise software. Understanding how to build your own form library gives you fine-grained control over validation logic, error handling, and user experience that off-the-shelf solutions might not provide.

objectives: Construct a reactive form state using Vue's ref and reactive APIs
Implement form validation logic with custom validator functions
Bind form inputs to reactive state using v-model directives
Control form submission behavior with event handlers
Render validation error messages conditionally in the template
Initialize and reset form state programmatically
Integrate form components with a parent application structure

steps.title: Import Vue and reactive from Vue
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the reactive function from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both Vue and reactive from the 'vue' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing multiple items from a module
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and reactive function are available for use in your component.
successCriteria: Vue and reactive are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported something, but make sure you're importing both Vue and reactive from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: import both Vue and reactive from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create main FormLibrary component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named FormLibrary with a default export. The component should return a template with a single root div element.
steps.hint: Use the Vue component structure you've learned. Start with 'export default' followed by the component definition.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a basic Vue component structure for FormLibrary that can be built upon in later steps.
successCriteria: FormLibrary component is created with default export, has a name property, and returns a template with a single root div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have: 1) default export, 2) name property set to 'FormLibrary', and 3) template with a single root div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Remember to use the Vue component format with export default, a name property, and a template.

steps.title: Initialize form state with reactive
steps.instruction: Inside the FormLibrary component, initialize a reactive form object with empty values for 'name' and 'email' fields.
steps.hint: Use the reactive function to create a reactive object with name and email properties set to empty strings.
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive form object with name and email properties is created inside the component's setup function.
successCriteria: The component contains a reactive object with name and email properties initialized to empty strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using reactive() and including both name and email fields with empty string values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form object isn't properly initialized. Remember to use reactive() and include both name and email fields.

steps.title: Define handleInput handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named handleInput that takes two parameters: fieldName and value. The function should update the form state object by setting the property with fieldName to value.
steps.hint: Create a regular function inside setup() that updates the reactive form object using bracket notation.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleInput function is defined that can update any field in the form state object.
successCriteria: handleInput function is defined with two parameters and updates the form state object using bracket notation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it takes two parameters and updates the form state object correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleInput function is not properly defined. It should take fieldName and value parameters and update the form state.

steps.title: Add form element with submit handler
steps.instruction: In the template, add a <form> element inside the <div> and bind its submit event to the handleSubmit function using @submit.
steps.hint: Use @submit.prevent to prevent the default form submission behavior and call handleSubmit.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a form with submit handler
<form @submit.prevent="handleSubmit">
  <!-- form content will go here -->
</form>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains a <form> element with its submit event bound to handleSubmit.
successCriteria: A <form> element is added inside the <div> with @submit.prevent="handleSubmit".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the form element, but make sure to bind the submit event to handleSubmit using @submit.prevent.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form element or submit handler binding is missing. Add a <form> with @submit.prevent="handleSubmit" inside the <div>.

steps.title: Add name input field
steps.instruction: Inside the form element, add an input field for the name with v-model binding to form.name.
steps.hint: Use <input type="text" v-model="form.name"> to create a text input bound to the form.name property.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: input field with v-model
<input type="text" v-model="form.email">
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have a text input field that updates the form.name property when typed into.
successCriteria: An input element with type="text" and v-model="form.name" is added inside the form.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input, but check that it has both type="text" and v-model="form.name" attributes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input field is missing or doesn't have the correct v-model binding to form.name.

steps.title: Add email input field
steps.instruction: Add an email input field inside the form element, using v-model to bind it to form.email.
steps.hint: Add an <input> element with type='email' and v-model='form.email' after the name input field.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding another input field
<input type="email" v-model="form.email" placeholder="Enter email">
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have two input fields: one for name and one for email, both bound to the reactive form state.
successCriteria: An email input field with v-model='form.email' is added to the form template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input field, but make sure it has type='email' and v-model='form.email'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The email input field is missing or incorrectly configured. Add an <input> element with type='email' and v-model='form.email'.

steps.title: Add submit button
steps.instruction: Inside the form element, add a submit button with type='submit' and the text 'Submit'.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element with type='submit' attribute inside the form, after the existing input fields.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a submit button to a form
<button type="submit">Submit Form</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have a submit button that users can click to submit the form.
successCriteria: A submit button with type='submit' and text 'Submit' is added inside the form element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has type='submit' and the text 'Submit'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The submit button is missing or incorrect. Add a <button type="submit">Submit</button> inside the form.

steps.title: Display current form values
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element below the form to display the current values of form.name and form.email.
steps.hint: Use a paragraph tag with text interpolation to show both values. You can access them directly from the form reactive object.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying reactive values in Vue

Name: {{ form.name }}, Email: {{ form.email }}
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph showing the current form values appears below the form.
successCriteria: A paragraph element displays both form.name and form.email values using Vue's template syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but it might not be displaying both form values correctly. Make sure you're using the correct template syntax to show form.name and form.email.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph displaying form values is missing or incorrect. Add a paragraph element below the form that shows both form.name and form.email values.

steps.title: Integrate validation in submit handler
steps.instruction: Update the handleSubmit function to call validateForm and show an alert if the form is invalid.
steps.hint: Inside handleSubmit, call validateForm and check its return value. If invalid, show an alert and prevent form submission.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleSubmit function will now validate the form before submission and alert the user if validation fails.
successCriteria: handleSubmit calls validateForm, checks its return value, and shows an alert when the form is invalid.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure handleSubmit calls validateForm and shows an alert when validation fails.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleSubmit function needs to call validateForm and show an alert if the form is invalid. Check your implementation.
